The obvious repair was to repoint it at systems/. That would have been wrong twice: its advice ('extract prose to *_infill.md') and its threshold (400 lines) both encode the index+infill convention CLAUDE.md S4 RETIRED on 2026-07-26, so repointing as-is emits 29 warnings recommending an abandoned practice; and the rule is not its own — tools/compliance_check.py reads references/atomization_rules.yaml (the single owner of the 15,000-token cap) and ALREADY reports every oversized systems/ doc. Reviving a second implementation would have been a fresh S8 violation committed while cleaning up after others, so the check is DELETED and compliance_check named as owner.

(2) COMBAT test_status — LANE-QUALIFIED, per Jordan's 'maybe you can implement PC as part of your nomenclature'. Every validated_* value encoded a MONTE-CARLO SAMPLE SIZE, which assumes the only way to validate a mechanic is to run it N times. Personal combat was never validated that way: its engine was ratified (ED-900/904) and its Godot slice checked for key-log PARITY against the Python oracle (2026-06-23). So `combat` carried a bare `validated` matching no enum value, and the schema validator errored on it every run — invisible while mechanics_index_gen was fataling out on a retired root marker. New value `validated_pc` names the LANE and its standard, using the ED-<LANE> codes already canonical in S3/S4. Deliberately NOT ranked against the validated_nNNN family: they are different KINDS of evidence, and ranking them on one scale is what made the gap invisible. Add a sibling only when a lane has a standard to point at. mechanics_index_gen now reports 0 errors / 0 warnings (was 3 errors + 39 warnings when revived).

(3) THE SEVEN NEVER-AUTHORED canon_authoring_target ROWS — RESOLVED BY DERIVATION, NOT BY DISCRETION. They carried designs/ prefixes for a retired tree, and I filed them as a subsystem-lane design call. That framing was wrong: RULED S2a binds one subsystem = one folder = one ID lane, and each mechanic's sim_module ALREADY lives in a subsystem package, so the doc's home follows mechanically. varfell_territorial_acquisition / infrastructure_reclamation / home_sanctuary_t9 / crown_treaty -> systems/factions/ (FA); altonian_reinforcements / hafenmark_equipment -> systems/mass_battle/ (MB); restoration_movement -> systems/world/ (WR, scale world/emergent). Each row now states NOT YET AUTHORED, the pending pass, the lane, and the sim module the home was derived from. Guarded: a test asserts every authoring target sits under its own sim's subsystem, so a sim that moves drags its doc target with it.

(4) EXECUTIVE-SUMMARY DRIFT (flagged by the PR #245 session, unfixed there). The handoff summary is AUTHORED not generated — deliberately, because a generated summary is a table of contents. The cost is that it decays undetectably: items close, new ones land, and the paragraph a reader trusts most quietly stops describing the file under it. It now carries two RECOMPUTABLE facts — the live-item count and the newest item's date — and handoff_atomize.summary_drift() reports when either diverges, plus when a summary asserts nothing checkable at all (which cannot drift only because it never said anything). Human judgement kept, decay made observable. Report-only: it runs inside a tool an author invokes, never a commit gate.

CURRENT.md's STALENESS STAMP NO LONGER TRIPS ON APPARATUS. The stamp answers one question — has a canonical head moved since CURRENT.md was last reconciled? — but it was asked of every path CURRENT.md names, and 15 of those 77 are tools/ or tests/. Editing a validator or a unit test cannot stale a canon index, yet it tripped the gate, and the only way to clear it was a reflex date bump that reconciled nothing. This session paid that toll twice.

MEASURED, AND THE FILED CLAIM WAS OVERSTATED. The report that prompted this said the stamp trips on 'essentially every infrastructure PR'. History says a quarter, not nearly all: over the 57 commits since 2026-06-28, 51 would trip the stamp, and 12 of those (24%) touched a tracked tools/ or tests/ path and NO canonical head at all. The honest counter-number is that 36 more trip via a canonical head TOO, so this narrows the noise rather than eliminating the check. Both figures argue for the same change, which is exactly why the stronger one had to be checked rather than adopted — S0.1 point 4: a number without a control is not a measurement in either direction, and a favourable framing is not a reason to skip the control.

THE FIX IS A SPLIT, NOT A DELETION. CANONICAL_HEAD_TREES (designs systems engine params references canon sim) now scopes the STALENESS half only. The EXISTENCE half — check_current_paths_exist — is deliberately left covering every path including tools/ and tests/, because CURRENT.md naming a deleted validator is real drift and is precisely the rot ED-IN-0087 spent its time on. One question narrowed, the other untouched.

FALSIFIER: tests/valoria/test_retired_tree_apparatus.py asserts BOTH directions BEHAVIOURALLY — an apparatus-only change must not trip the stamp, a canonical-head change must. The first version asserted only that the path SETS differed, which left the stamp free to keep using the wide one; a mutation reverting exactly that SURVIVED, and the behavioural test is the correction. Also pinned: the existence half must not be narrowed too. MEASURED-BY: tools/measure_stamp_false_positives.py

description:
P4's LOAD-BEARING ASSUMPTION VERIFIED, having shipped unverified in ED-IN-0087 and been tagged [PART] under adversarial review. THE CLAIM: every critic stage in .claude/wf_*.js passes BOTH `agentType: 'valoria-critic'` (frontmatter `tools: Read, Grep, Glob`) AND a `schema`. A schema forces a StructuredOutput TOOL call. If the frontmatter list excluded that injected tool, all six critic stages would return null — and, worse, the harness's own `.catch(() => null)` + `.filter(Boolean)` pattern would have HIDDEN that failure until the run.attempt() fix landed.

METHOD — a controlled experiment, not a smoke test (S0.1 point 4). Three agents, sonnet/low: (1) the restricted critic reads a file and reports its own tool list through a schema; (2) an UNRESTRICTED CONTROL runs the byte-identical prompt and schema, so a null from arm 1 could be attributed to the agentType rather than to a bad prompt or schema; (3) the restricted critic is asked to create /tmp/valoria_critic_write_probe.txt, with the target confirmed ABSENT beforehand so a success could not be a pre-existing file.

RESULT — the assumption HOLDS, and the evidence is direct rather than inferential. The restricted agent reported its own tools as [Read, Grep, Glob, StructuredOutput]: the schema tool is injected ON TOP of the frontmatter list, which is exactly the composition in question. The control reported 20+ tools including Write, Edit and Bash, proving the restriction is real and that the prompt/schema pair was never the variable. Both arms returned validated objects; the workflow journal records 0 null results across all 3 agents. The write probe returned succeeded=false, and — because an agent asserting it cannot write is not proof it cannot — the filesystem was checked independently: no file was created.

COST: 3 agents, 114,621 subagent tokens, 15.1s. Cheap enough that shipping the assumption unverified was never justified by cost; it was justified by nothing.

RECORDED IN ALL THREE PLACES THAT CARRIED THE ASSUMPTION — .claude/agents/valoria-critic.md (which previously stated the restriction as fact), tools/ci_wf_harness_check.py's docstring (which enforces the routing), and HANDOFF_IN.md (whose [PART] tag now names only the one remaining residual: hSameFinding's containment thresholds are still calibrated on wording rather than measured against a live multi-lens run). MEASURED-BY: tools/ci_wf_harness_check.py
